item.title: Nvidia says no return for ousted CEO, reports revenue boom - AFP.com
item.description:
AI summary: Nvidia said on Tuesday that it will not reinstate Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO last week over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and that interim CEO Colette Kress is running the company as "business as usual." The company also reported that its third-quarter revenue doubled to more than $115 billion, beating expectations, and Kress forecast 75 percent revenue growth in the next fiscal year. The article notes that Nvidia has lost $700 billion in market value since the scandal broke, and that new US export restrictions on AI chips and a Huang hearing with US lawmakers on December 1 remain sources of uncertainty.

item.title: Nvidia chair closes the door on Jensen Huang comeback; analysts don’t push on China/Singapore black box - Fortune
item.description:
AI summary: Nvidia's board said it will not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and refused to discuss the circumstances of his November 12 resignation, which followed disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, while the company beat revenue estimates with $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue and raised its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to about 75%. For NVDA holders, the matters that bear on the outlook are the reported SEC civil probe into whether Nvidia misled investors, the criminal investigation into Singapore-based Megaspeed over possible diversion of chips to China, and the new CEO search, all of which the call largely left unaddressed by analysts.
